test.title: login API returns a token
test.error:
Error: expect(received).toBe(expected) // Object.is equality
Expected: 200
Received: 423

triage.reason: The API returned HTTP 423 (Locked), the demo API's account-lockout response after repeated failed login attempts — not a 401/403 credential rejection and not a server error. The test's request and assertion are reasonable, and the endpoint is clearly alive, so this points to shared/external account state on the public practicesoftwaretesting API (locked by earlier runs, parallel tests, or other users) rather than an app defect. The lockout lasts a cool-down window, which explains why all 3 attempts failed identically. Secondary possibility: 'pass123' is stale test data whose repeated failures produced the lock, which would make it a broken script — but 423 alone does not prove wrong credentials.
triage.evidence: Error line: "Expected: 200 / Received: 423" at `expect(response.status()).toBe(200);` against `data: { email: 'customer3@practicesoftwaretesting.com', password: 'pass123' }` — 423 Locked is the lockout status, not an invalid-credential or server-failure status.
triage.next_step: Wait out the lockout window (or reset/seed a dedicated login user), then re-run just this test with `--repeat-each=1` and log the response body; if it returns 401 instead of 200, the credentials `customer3@practicesoftwaretesting.com` / `pass123` are stale and must be updated (reclassify as broken script).

triage.reason: The add-to-cart action demonstrably worked — the nav cart badge in the failure snapshot reads "1" — yet the success notification is absent from the page entirely. The accessibility tree contains no toast text at all, not even a reworded variant, so this is not a stale locator matching changed copy. The failure reproduced on all 3 attempts with the full 5s timeout consumed, ruling out a transient/auto-dismiss race. The page is explicitly in "Bug Hunting Mode" and shows other seeded defects ("Contakt", "Reltded products", Home link pointing at #/contact), consistent with a deliberately suppressed confirmation message. Confidence is medium rather than high because the snapshot is one point in time and I could not read app source to verify the message string ever existed.
triage.evidence: Error line: "Locator: getByText('Product added to shopping cart.') / Expected: visible / Error: element(s) not found". triage.next_step: Re-run the test with --trace on and scrub the trace timeline right after the `Add to cart` click to confirm no notification element is ever attached to the DOM; if confirmed, file an app bug that the cart badge increments without showing the "Product added to shopping cart." confirmation.

The real app request carries a path/query the glob doesn't match (e.g. `/products?between=price,1,100&page=0` or `/products/search`), so the live API response was rendered. Because the app was never given an empty list, the missing "There are no products found." text is not app misbehaviour — the test's route pattern (and therefore its premise) is out of date/wrong. The hint about a bad locator is a symptom, not the cause.
triage.evidence: Test code: `await page.route('**/products', (route) => route.fulfill({ status: 200, json: { data: [] } }));` vs. the failure-time page content: `- 'link "ECO Combination Pliers CO₂: A B C D E $14.15"'` and `- navigation "Pagination"` — real products rendered, so the empty-list mock did not apply. Error: `expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed ... element(s) not found`.
triage.next_step: Run the test with `PWDEBUG`/`--trace on` (or log `page.on('request')`) to capture the exact products request URL, then widen the route glob to match it (e.g. `**/products?**` or `**/products*`) and re-run to confirm the empty-state message appears.

triage.reason: The test waits for a response whose request method is 'QUERY', a method the shop does not use for its product filter (it filters via a GET to /products). The predicate can never match, so page.waitForResponse hangs until the 30s test timeout, deterministically on all 3 attempts. Meanwhile the app behaved correctly: the accessibility tree shows the Pliers checkbox as [checked] and the product list already showing the filtered Pliers products, so neither the UI nor the API is broken, and the repeatable failure rules out flakiness.
triage.evidence: Predicate at line 16: "(response) => response.request().method() === 'QUERY' && response.url().endsWith('/products')" with error "page.waitForResponse: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded." while the page shows 'checkbox "Pliers" [checked]' and links for "Combination Pliers" / "Pliers".
triage.next_step: Record the network traffic for the category-filter click (Playwright trace or DevTools Network) to confirm the real request, then change the predicate to match it — e.g. (response) => response.request().method() === 'GET' && response.url().includes('/products') && response.url().includes('by_category').

triage.reason: The timeout is on the response predicate, not on the app. The accessibility tree proves the action worked: the Pliers checkbox is [checked] and the product grid is already filtered to plier products. The test nevertheless never saw a matching response because isProductsQuery requires method === 'QUERY' and a URL ending exactly in '/products' — the shop filters with a normal GET whose URL carries query params, so the predicate can never match. Same failure on all 3 attempts rules out flakiness. (Note: the brand list renders as 'Brand name 1..10', so the test data 'ForgeFlex Tools' is also absent — possibly a separate app/data bug, but step 2 was never reached.)
triage.evidence: Error: page.waitForResponse: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded. at line 17 `const categoryResponse = page.waitForResponse(isProductsQuery);` with predicate `response.request().method() === 'QUERY' && response.url().endsWith('/products')`, while the page shows `checkbox "Pliers" [checked] [active] [ref=e83]` and filtered results `heading "Combination Pliers"`.
triage.next_step: Run the test with network logging (page.on('request'/'response')) or open DevTools Network while checking the Pliers filter, then rewrite isProductsQuery to match the real call — e.g. `response.request().method() === 'GET' && response.url().includes('/products')` — and also re-check that a 'ForgeFlex Tools' brand filter actually exists before step 2.

triage.reason: The add-to-cart action itself succeeded — the failure-time accessibility tree shows the cart badge as "cart ... 1" — yet the standard confirmation toast never appeared within 5s, and it failed identically on all 3 attempts (so not timing/flake). The same snapshot shows the app is running in "🐛 Bug Hunting Mode" with other visibly mutated strings ("Contakt", "Reltded products", an unlabeled quantity button), which indicates injected app-side defects rather than an outdated test. The test's expectation of a "Product added to shopping cart." confirmation after a successful add is reasonable, so the missing/altered notification is the app misbehaving. (A deliberately reworded toast string would technically also make the locator stale, so this is not 100% clear-cut.)
triage.evidence: Error line: `expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed  Locator: getByText('Product added to shopping cart.') ... element(s) not found`; page snapshot at failure: `menuitem "cart": link "cart": /url: "#/checkout" - text:  1` (item was added) plus `🐛 Bug Hunting Mode - Find & Report Bugs!` and mutated labels `menuitem "Contakt"`, `heading "Reltded products"`.
triage.next_step: Manually add "Combination Pliers" to the cart in chromium against the same build and watch the toast region (and the DOM/console) — confirm whether no notification is rendered at all (app bug to file) or whether the toast text has been changed to a mutated string, in which case update the locator in addToCart() to match the actual message.
